subject: Turn ExtremeGC into largest-class-first semantic compaction

body.observed_failure_mode: V5 reclaimed only about 0.54 GiB while emitting large numbers of individual DeletionProofs for tiny bytecode/cache directories. Correctness is intact, but proof/I-O granularity is too fine for a 30 GiB deficit.
required_actions: Measure reclaim classes by parent/class and expected bytes before walking leaf caches; prioritize the largest recoverable classes first.
Delete cache/build classes at the highest safe semantic parent instead of one __pycache__ leaf at a time.

Introduce a bounded batch DeletionProof or Merkle-rooted deletion receipt: one receipt can bind many homogeneous regenerable deletions while retaining sampled paths, byte totals, class, policy, and recovery source.
Keep canonical source, active envs, current authority, secrets, and active Run8 state protected; do not restore filename allowlist conservatism.

Classify Docker unavailable as its own ResourceGraph state. Determine installed-vs-stopped-vs-broken-vs-space-starved rather than treating all as unavailable; if local authority permits and Docker Desktop is installed but stopped, activate it and immediately expose/prune reclaimable builder/image/container state.
Feed recovered capacity back into scheduler admission so heavy Docker/build/model tasks turn on as soon as the resource envelope allows, not only on next restart.
body.compounding_rule: A GC epoch must report reclaimed_bytes / proof_bytes / scan_seconds / deletion_count / largest_classes. If leaf-proof overhead dominates reclaimed value, promote the parent class or batch proof next cycle.
